00100

2026
Interactive kinetic sculpture: collaborative robot arm, robotic hand, webcam, custom software
Gray Area, San Francisco

00100 is a collaborative robot, or cobot, installed in the front window of Gray Area in San Francisco. Cobots are designed to work safely alongside people in factories, laboratories, and classrooms, and their selling point is cooperation. Fitted with a humanoid left hand, this one has a single task: when its camera detects someone passing, the arm turns to find them and raises its middle finger.

It was trained in the cloud, where a virtual twin of the robot studied photographs of history’s most notorious middle fingers, from a baseball pitcher in 1886 to Johnny Cash at San Quentin, and refined its pose until it matched each one. On the robot itself, a small neural network picks out people in the camera’s view and keeps the hand aimed at the nearest. Around the corner, a vertical video on a monitor stripped down to its metal frame shows the twin learning each gesture, intercut with a 2,400-year history of the middle finger.

The gesture is crude by design. A machine marketed on its deference performs one of the oldest gestures of refusal, aimed with computational precision at whoever walks by, through a camera from the same family of tools that turns public life into data. A passerby who answers with a selfie completes the circuit: a camera watching a robot watching a person, all of it bound for the network.
